Management system — Bingkun Qi

Weekly feedback, chase-up, timetable changes, rosters and exports share one role model. This page shows anonymised screenshots of what already works — it does not open the production database.

A week in the system

A five-step loop from fill-in to export. Structure and screenshots only — no writable demo in phase 1.

  1. Subject fill-in — Batch-enter the week by class; fold columns and apply presets.
  2. Homeroom chase-up — See missing subjects and route reminders to teachers.
  3. Timetable requests — Teachers request moves/cancels; admins can apply immediately.
  4. Roster care — Keep students, classes and teaching assignments aligned.
  5. Export & audit — Print/CSV leave a trail; hours roll up by week.

Modules

Numbers 01–06 cover complete admin jobs we can show today. Screenshots come from a local anonymised demo database.

01

Weekly feedback fill-in

The subject-teacher path: filter class and students, Excel-style batch fill, fold secondary columns, apply multi-field presets.

02

Homeroom overview & chase-up

Missing subjects and students to watch, chase chips that name the subject teacher, plus print and chase CSV.

03

Timetable, moves and add-ons

Teachers request time changes, cancels or covers; admins can act immediately. Student timetable is covered as a role slice.

04

Administrative rosters

Students, classes and teaching assignments form the data triangle; admins can maintain enrolment and open a student timetable view.

05

Exams & homework

Exam entry and homework set/recording sit beside weekly feedback as the academic track.

No anonymised screenshots in this release (exam / homework pages still to capture from local demo).

06

Hours & export audit

Hours roll up from weekly templates and temp add-ons; teacher/homeroom print and CSV writes leave an export log.
